title: Alleged AI-Generated Papers Misuse Open Neuroimaging Data
source_used: The Scientist (first published at Retraction Watch)
key_facts: Dorothy Bishop, emeritus professor at the University of Oxford, found two 2026 papers in the Journal of Neurolinguistics that claim to analyse open brain-scan data from OpenNeuro.
She and Kathy Rastle of the University of London, whose data appear in one paper, believe the papers were AI-generated.
The papers contain errors about the datasets and numbers that do not match the data.
The first paper (May) was by Afzal Khan and Dawood Khan; the second (August) by Afzal Khan alone.
Elsevier, the publisher, says it is investigating; the journal's editor submitted its own inquiry findings to Elsevier.
Khan says he is engaging with the journal in good faith and said some analyses would be redone and a correction was being processed.
quote_evidence: “This is clearly some sort of AI that knows enough about a dataset to produce a plausible paper that purports to use it,” Bishop said.
Elsevier told her that it would investigate, but that it “may take considerable time.”
why_it_matters_hint: Shows how open data can be cited to make fake AI papers look credible.
notes: Alleged: the AI-generation claim is the two scientists' belief, not a finding by the journal or Elsevier.
